security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel accesses the eithreshold CSR on a hart implementing Smidctrl or Ssidctrl, where eithreshold is no longer included in scope and its interrupt-threshold function is replaced by the new mithreshold CSR with different semantics (applies to both major and minor interrupt identities, not just major).
security_spec.summary: Removal of eithreshold from Smidctrl/Ssidctrl scope means kernel code touching eithreshold CSR on these systems encounters undefined CSR access, risking illegal-instruction traps; kernel must migrate to mithreshold which differs in applying thresholds to both major and minor interrupt identities.

findings.finding: IMSIC_EITHRESHOLD is defined as 0x72, which is an IMSIC sub-selector for the indirect CSR_ISELECT/CSR_IREG access mechanism defined by the AIA spec, NOT a dedicated CSR at 0x352. The Smidctrl spec change removing the dedicated eithreshold CSR (0x352) does not affect the AIA-defined IMSIC indirect register file.

imsic_local_delivery() enables/disables interrupt delivery by writing IMSIC_ENABLE_EITHRESHOLD (0)/IMSIC_DISABLE_EITHRESHOLD (1) to the IMSIC indirect register at ISELECT=0x72 via imsic_csr_write(), which writes to CSR_ISELECT then CSR_IREG. This is correct AIA-specified indirect access, not a direct CSR 0x352 access. No vulnerability.

The indirect access helper imsic_csr_write() routes ALL IMSIC register accesses through CSR_ISELECT (S-mode: CSR_SISELECT at 0x150, M-mode: CSR_MISELECT at 0x350) followed by CSR_IREG. The sub-selector 0x72 selects the IMSIC eithreshold register within the AIA indirect register file. This mechanism is defined by the AIA specification and is architecturally distinct from the dedicated CSR at 0x352 that Smidctrl removes.

KVM VM-exit save path: guest eithreshold is saved from the IMSIC VS-file via CSR_VSISELECT/CSR_VSIREG (VS-level indirect access), not via a dedicated CSR 0x352. Correctly uses the AIA-specified indirect register mechanism for virtualized IMSIC state. The Smidctrl CSR removal does not affect VS-level IMSIC indirect registers.
KVM VM-exit save path (non-clearing variant): reads guest eithreshold from IMSIC VS-file via indirect CSR_VSISELECT/CSR_VSIREG. Same AIA-compliant indirect mechanism, not a dedicated CSR access.

KVM VM-entry restore path: restores guest eithreshold into IMSIC VS-file via imsic_vs_csr_write(), which writes to CSR_VSISELECT then CSR_VSIREG. The Smidctrl change to dedicated CSR 0x352 has no bearing on the VS-level IMSIC indirect register mechanism.
KVM IMSIC VS-file zero-out: writes 0 to VS-level IMSIC eithreshold register via indirect CSR_VSISELECT/CSR_VSIREG during VS-file initialization. No dedicated CSR 0x352 involved.
KVM SW-file update: atomic write of eithreshold from guest MRIF to shadow SW-file. This is a software-in-memory operation copying the shadowed register state, with no CSR access at all.

KVM topei computation: reads the in-memory shadow eithreshold field (software MRIF) to compute the top external interrupt. This is a software data structure access, not a CSR access. No hardware CSR interaction at all.
KVM MRIF read-modify-write: atomic RMW on the in-memory shadow eithreshold field. Software-only operation on the MRIF data structure, no CSR access.
KVM VS-file register read/write dispatch: routes IMSIC_EITHRESHOLD accesses to imsic_vs_csr_read/write which use the indirect CSR_VSISELECT/CSR_VSIREG mechanism. No dedicated CSR 0x352 access.
